channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI Speeds Patching, Raises Outage Risks: Expert
item.description: A wave of disruptions across banking, travel and government systems may not stem from one sweeping cyberattack says Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan. He joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how AI is helping uncover more vulnerabilities, and forcing companies to patch them faster, increasing the risk of errors. He says the answer is resilience built into systems from the start. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: One Secret to the Success of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’: Veteran Staff
item.description: Nearly 1,000 Rockstar employees have been at the company for a decade or more
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: Anthropic IPO Tests AI Investor Appetite
item.description: Renaissance Capital’s Avery Marquez joins Bloomberg Open Interest to weigh Anthropic’s valuation and growth prospects. She also discusses what early trading could signal for future IPOs, including OpenAI’s path to the public markets. ( (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Share Slump Nearly Erases IPO Pop
item.description: Anthropic PBC shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors’ faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history. Gene Munster, Managing Partner at Deepwater Asset Management and Ted Mortonson, Managing Director: Technology at Baird, discuss AI trade volatility and how Nvidia and Anthropic have reshaped the AI narrative. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Founder to Donate to Trump Accounts Following IPO, Bessent Says
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that an Anthropic PBC founder will make a donation to Trump accounts in the next few weeks, after the artificial intelligence firm’s initial public offering this week made its founders multi-billionaires.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: Anthropic's IPO Is 'Monstrous,' General Catalyst’s Namburi Says
item.description: Madhu Namburi, managing director and co-head of the creation fund at General Catalyst, discusses Anthropic’s "monstrous" IPO after the stock rallied 17% on its first day before moving back toward its $86 listing price. Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Namburi says Anthropic can withstand the market volatility and the stock has a lot more potential. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ING’s $500 Million Data Center Loan Auction Stalls on Low Bids
item.description: Dutch bank ING received muted demand for a roughly $500 million auction of data center loans ahead of its deadline, prompting the lender to seek individual sales of the debt instead.
item.dc:creator: Jeannine Amodeo, Reshmi Basu and Carmen Arroyo

item.title: What Caused the US Tech Outages? Why Experts Expect More
item.description: A series of technology outages that began on Nov. 11 spawned a collective freak-out across the US. Breakdowns that knocked out Microsoft Corp. software, snarled air travel and disrupted the work of the National Security Agency prompted consumers to panic-buy emergency supplies as if these were signs of an impending cataclysm. Certainly, cybersecurity experts say, they were a sign of things to come, as old technology increasingly needs to be replaced.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Stone

item.title: AI Credit Risk Gauges Worsen as Tech Selloff Roils Markets
item.description: Gauges of credit risk rose for some of the biggest hyperscalers and chip makers while their bonds weakened on Friday, as the wobbling AI trade spurred volatility in global markets.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua

item.title: UBS's Lovell Sees AI CapEx at Risk of 5%-10% Cut
item.description: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says regulatory risks could cut AI capital spending estimates by 5% to 10%. UBS remains positive on the long-term AI opportunity but is focusing on companies with financial strength and a clear path to monetization, she says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investor Worry Has Come to a Head, Says Allspring’s Miletti
item.description: Ann Miletti, global head of equity investments at Allspring, says investors have begun questioning AI, the interest rate environment and the economy, with all of the worries rolling into one in the market selloff. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Everybody’s Business: Relax. It’s Probably Not a Cyberattack
item.description:
Flight grounding, banking disruptions and outages at the National Security Agency, Apple and Microsoft — a series of online disruptions are causing widespread panic, as people speculate if the US is under some kind of attack.
Bloomberg's Jordan Robertson joins Max Chafkin and Stacey Vanek Smith on the Everybody’s Business podcast to discuss AI’s role in the recent outages. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: USTR Greer on Chip Curbs, Rare Earths, US-China Trade
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer discusses US chip controls, talks between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on rare earths, and the potential for an extension of the US-China trade agreement. He speaks with Annmarie Hordern on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Polish Stocks Lead European Losses After Russian Airspace Breach
item.description: Polish stocks were the worst performers in Europe as a Russian incursion into the country’s airspace reminded investors of the geopolitical risks stemming from the war in neighboring Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski

item.title: Novartis CEO: AI Could Cut Drug Development Time by Years
item.description: Novartis CEO Vasant Narasimhan says artificial intelligence could help cut drug-development times from 12 years to eight and significantly improve the odds of bringing new medicines to market. Narasimhan, who also sits on Anthropic’s board, tells Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua on "The Pulse" that AI is already helping Novartis speed up clinical trials, analyze data and identify new drug candidates. He also discusses the company’s growth outlook, drug pricing in Europe and the US, and AI regulation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Tumbles Near IPO Price in Second Day of Trading
item.description: Anthropic shares fell on their second day of trading, coming close to the stock’s IPO price. The Claude chatbot maker’s shares tumbled more than 10% in premarket trading in New York earlier Friday. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: S&P 500 Sinks Into Correction as Nvidia-Led AI Selloff Continues
item.description: A slide in the S&P 500 Index on Friday pushed it into a correction territory after a string of disappointing Big Tech earnings and scandal at Nvidia Corp. eroded confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Judy Lagrou

item.title: Emerging Market Stocks on Cusp of Bear Market as AI Rout Expands
item.description: Emerging-market stocks extended their declines for a seventh day on Friday, with MSCI’s equity index on the cusp of a bear market amid a continued selloff in global tech shares.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu, Prima Wirayani and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: Retail Investors Dive Into Both Sides of Anthropic
item.description: Retail traders rushed to buy — and sell — Anthropic PBC shares in one of the busiest market debuts on record Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz and Bernard Goyder

item.title: SpaceX Wraps Up $32 Billion of AI Chip Debt at Yields Topping 8%
item.description: SpaceX’s $32 billion debt deal to fund its access to chips may serve as a blueprint for similar transactions as the next wave of financing tied to the artificial intelligence boom gets underway. It is likely going to be costly for the companies borrowing.
item.dc:creator: Brian Smith, Davide Barbuscia and Caleb Mutua
